title: This video was edited with AI agent. But how?
talk_summary: A team built an open-source video-editing agent that drives a browser-based editor by having the LLM generate and execute TypeScript code against a programmatic composition API, rather than emitting JSON tool calls. It uses a doc-search tool (ripgrep) for context, samples rendered frames at 1 fps and feeds them to a visual-feedback 'discriminator' tool that must approve before final render, and ships an llms.txt plus template prompts to guide the agent.

takeaways.technique: Code-as-action instead of JSON tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent writes and runs code against a typed programmatic API rather than emitting structured JSON tool calls, which they argue is a better action representation for computers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having llm tool calling in code is much better than in Json

takeaways.what_they_do: After each execution step they sample the composition at 1 frame per second and pass frames to a separate visual-feedback tool acting as a discriminator; only on its green light does the agent proceed to render.
takeaways.evidence_quote: visual feedback tool can be sold as uh generator and discriminator like in famous gun architecture

takeaways.technique: Doc-search tool over ripgrep for on-demand context
takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated doc-search tool uses ripgrep to pull only relevant documentation when the agent needs extra context, instead of stuffing docs into the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: doc Search tool uses rck to pull the relevant information

takeaways.technique: llms.txt plus template prompts for agent onboarding
takeaways.what_they_do: They ship an llms.txt (robots.txt for agents) alongside specific template prompts so an agent can orient itself in the product without bespoke instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also shipped lm. txt which is essentially robots.txt but for agents

takeaways.technique: Remote GPU browser sessions per agent behind a load balancer
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent gets its own remote browser session over WebSocket, GPU-accelerated, with a load balancer in front, so heavy rendering is offloaded from the orchestrator host.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each agent can get the separate browser session which is GP view accelerated and of course there's a load balance load balancer behind
